title: Each partnership gets its own Primitive Instance, making individual deals separately configurable and separately retirable
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.1.2 lists four `Active` Integration Boost Instances — Kamino, Drift, Save and Lifinity — while the Primitive itself has one Global Activation Status. Each Instance carries its own full parameter set: Integration Partner Name, Reward Address, Chain, Cadence, Data Submission Format and Responsible Actor, Savings Rate Adjustment Strategy, and a customization slot (e.g. A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.2.1.1.x for Kamino).

The Instance is therefore the unit of a *commercial relationship*, not of a program type. That yields three practical properties: a new partner is onboarded by Invoking one more Instance rather than editing shared configuration; one partner's terms can differ from another's without exceptions or conditionals; and a single relationship can be Suspended or moved to Completed while the rest keep paying, because status lives per Instance.

It also makes each deal individually auditable. A reader can point at one address in the Artifact and see exactly which venue is being paid, on which chain, how often, and on whose measurement — rather than reconstructing it from a combined incentive budget.

The cost is duplication: four Instances repeat the same skeleton and the same Core Council Risk Advisor and API endpoint, so an ecosystem-wide change to those must be made in every Instance or pushed through the inherited base protocol.
description: Keel runs one Integration Boost Instance per venue — Kamino, Drift, Save, Lifinity — each with its own reward address, chain, cadence and tracking, all under a single Active Primitive.
